title: Hedgerow AI - escape hatch compatibility and parity scan
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
summary: Initial discovery to map Hedgerow AI's exit path from current hosted model provider, assess runtime compatibility (vLLM/TGI), and agree next steps for eval parity benchmarks and security docs. Customer is cost-sensitive, needs sub-100ms tokens for small requests and KVM cache reuse for chat-like flows. Strong interest in Dedicated with VPC for PII workloads.
next_steps: Maya to share pricing deck and Dedicated capacity SKU sheet
Jorge to run initial vLLM/TGI compatibility checklist and follow-up notes
Customer to send sample prompt set and small eval corpus by 2027-07-02
Schedule technical deep-dive and benchmarking session week of 2027-07-05

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-06-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Location: Zoom
Attendees:
 - Maya Chen (Redwood AE)
 - Jorge Alvarez (Redwood SE)
 - Priya Nair (Redwood SE)
 - Samir Patel (Hedgerow AI, Head of ML)
 - Lena Ortiz (Hedgerow AI, Infra)
 - Rafiq Khan (Hedgerow AI, CTO)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
Hedgerow looking for an escape hatch from current hosted provider, they use mix of OpenAI embeddings + Anthropic chat for generative edges. Primary worry: runtime parity (vLLM/TGI stacks), latency/cost at scale, and data residency for EU customers. They want a small pilot on Redwood Hosted, then test Dedicated with VPC for PII.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we have about 50 minutes so we can run through your current setup and then go into the compatibility bits, is that okay?
[00:05] Samir Patel: Yeah, thanks Maya. Quick note, apologies we have a hard stop at 3:50, we have an exec sync.
[00:09] Maya Chen: Got it. Quick intros? I think we all know each other names but we'll do it real fast.
[00:13] Lena Ortiz: Lena, Infra lead, I look after deployments and networking.
[00:16] Rafiq Khan: Rafiq, CTO.
[00:18] Samir Patel: Samir, head of ML.
[00:20] Jorge Alvarez: Jorge, solutions engineer at Redwood, I usually dig into runtime and perf.
[00:24] Priya Nair: Priya, I work on pilot programs and onboarding.
[00:27] Maya Chen: Great. Okay Samir, can you give us the current stack and the main reason you're evaluating an exit?
[00:32] Samir Patel: Sure. Right now we're on a mixed stack. Primary inference is hosted OpenAI for chat completions and embeddings for search. We also have a smaller portion of Anthropic for safety-focused responses. For self-hosted we use vLLM on GCS instances for some internal tooling, and we're experimenting with TGI on a couple of GPU spots. The main driver is cost predictability — our OpenAI spend spiked Q1 and we had a lot of tail latency on longer chats — and we need region-level data residency for EU enterprise customers. Also pricing leakage when we hit token bursts.
[01:06] Maya Chen: Makes sense. When you say tail latency, what magnitude are we talking? 95th/99th numbers?
[01:11] Samir Patel: 95th on short prompts is fine, like 60-80ms per token for our small gen. But on multi-turn longer context with KV cache reuse, 99th can hit 500ms or even up to 900 depending on the model and concurrency.
[01:26] Jorge Alvarez: And are you using KV cache and prefix caching in vLLM today or is that earlier stage?
[01:31] Samir Patel: We have a crude KV cache in vLLM for internal dev flows, but in prod with OpenAI we rely on their session logic. Our issue is getting the same cache semantics when we try to self-host.
[01:43] Priya Nair: Are you running quantized models anywhere or is it full-fp16?
[01:46] Samir Patel: Mostly fp16. We did a quick int8 run in a POC but quality drop was noticeable for our legal summarization tail cases.
[01:56] Lena Ortiz: On infra constraints we need VPC peering, SAML SSO, and KMS integration. SOC2 is already table stakes.
[02:04] Maya Chen: Good callouts. Redwood Dedicated supports customer VPC and KMS/HSM integrations — we can supply SOC2 artifacts and our private deployment has options for on-prem if you need air-gapped.
[02:15] Rafiq Khan: For the dedicated option, is there any network egress pattern that would cause extra latency for EU customers? Our latency SLO is aggressive.
[02:22] Jorge Alvarez: If you pick a region close to your EU customers we can meet low latency. Dedicated gives you pinned hosts and consistent token throughput. Also our smart routing will keep traffic local when you opt for multi-region.
[02:34] Samir Patel: The other blocker is runtime compatibility. We run a lot of custom operators in vLLM and some tokenizer tweaks — will Redwood accept model artifacts produced by our TGI training?
[02:45] Jorge Alvarez: Short answer — usually yes, but it depends. We have onboarding paths for TGI artifacts and vLLM checkpoints, but sometimes conversion is needed for kernel compatibility. Common issues: custom attention op names, shard metadata, and quantization table formats. We can run a conversion pass and flag mismatches.
[03:02] Samir Patel: Okay, could you run that conversion probe for a small model? Maybe send a checklist so our infra folks can package the artifact correctly.
[03:09] Jorge Alvarez: Yes, I can. We'll need a sample model artifact and a small corpus for eval parity. If you send the vLLM checkpoint and the tokenizer config, we'll run a dry compatibility pass and report back.
[03:19] Priya Nair: And on the behavior parity side, do you have a process for aligning outputs — like control of sampling seeds, temperature mapping, and logit biases?
[03:28] Jorge Alvarez: We expose deterministic options and can map sampling parameters. For parity we typically run a batched eval with same prompt set and compare n-gram overlap, BLEU isn't perfect but we do multiple metrics including instruction-following score and hallucination checks.
[03:43] Samir Patel: Great. On evaluation we care about two buckets: semantic parity for our SLAs and cost per token. We run a 10k prompt suite for nightly regression; not sure if you'd want the whole thing for initial probe.
[03:56] Maya Chen: For an initial probe we'd ask for a subset, 400–800 prompts that represent the heavy hitters and the failure modes. That keeps the run manageable and quicker to iterate.
[04:06] Samir Patel: We'll pick 500 that have long contexts and tricky legal text.
[04:11] Lena Ortiz: Security question — log retention and PII. We can't have logs stored outside EU for some customers, is that doable?
[04:18] Maya Chen: Yes, with Redwood Private or Dedicated in EU-region we can ensure logs are kept in-region and integrate with your KMS. We can also configure token-level redaction for sensitive fields.
[04:29] Rafiq Khan: What about audit logs and read-only RBAC for our security team?
[04:33] Jorge Alvarez: We have detailed audit logs and RBAC. It integrates with SSO and we can set read-only roles. We'll share an excerpt of our audit schema in the security packet.
[04:43] Samir Patel: Pricing. Quick thing — our spend profile: about 15M tokens/month, mix of embeddings and chat, spikes up to 50M in campaign windows. We need predictable unit economics more than lowest floor price.
[04:58] Maya Chen: Understood. Dedicated contracts have commit bands and burst allowances. For hosted we do committed usage discounts that smooth spikes. I'll send the SKU sheet in follow up.
[05:09] Lena Ortiz: Any vendor lock-in clauses? We don't want to migrate and find ourselves stuck.
[05:13] Maya Chen: Redwood's export policy allows you to pull model logs and artifacts. For Dedicated/Private you manage keys and backups. We won't hold model artifacts hostage.
[05:22] Samir Patel: Back to runtime — you mentioned kernel selection earlier; in practice how do you ensure low variance for multi-turn chat?
[05:29] Jorge Alvarez: We profile sequence length distribution and pick kernel layouts that minimize memory copies and cache thrash. Also continuous batching is tuned per-host. For multi-turn chat, prefix caching and KV reuse are critical — we have heuristics to preserve KV format compatible with vLLM in many cases.
[05:47] Samir Patel: Do you support distributed KV across hosts or is it single-host binding?
[05:51] Jorge Alvarez: Currently KV is single-host bound per session for performance but we offer sticky routing so sessions remain on the same host. For bigger state, we can integrate a dedicated cache layer.
[06:03] Rafiq Khan: How do you measure quality regressions when changing quantization profiles? We saw a drop when we moved to int8 on some summarization tasks.
[06:11] Jorge Alvarez: We run quality monitoring tied to prompt sets and A/B test quant profiles. If quality drifts beyond a threshold we flag and auto-rollback. You can pick conservative quant profiles for legal/PII flows.
[06:24] Samir Patel: Good. Is there a playbook for moving from hosted (OpenAI) to Hosted Redwood first and then Dedicated? We're thinking staged routings while we validate parity.
[06:34] Priya Nair: A common path is stage 1: Redwood Hosted pilot, stage 2: run parity benchmarks and small traffic mirroring, stage 3: Dedicated pilot with VPC and keys, stage 4: full cutover. That reduces risk.
[06:47] Maya Chen: Exactly. We can do canary percentage routing and automatic fallback to your previous provider if latency or quality drops.
[06:55] Samir Patel: On the subject of mirroring, how much overhead does mirroring add? We want to mirror 10% of traffic for a week.
[07:01] Jorge Alvarez: Mirroring is lightweight for sync requests, but for gen requests you pay per-token for the mirrored calls. For 10% it should be manageable; we can quantify in the pricing sheet.
[07:12] Lena Ortiz: About SLOs — do you have published latency SLOs and uptime SLA?
[07:17] Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated comes with an SLA for uptime and per-token latency targets at certain commit levels. Hosted has published 99.9% uptime and latency profiles per model.
[07:27] Samir Patel: Are there any known incompatibilities with TGI artifacts containing custom layers?
[07:31] Jorge Alvarez: Custom layers are the tricky ones. If they rely on custom CUDA kernels you might need to recompile or we replicate behavior via shim ops. For many TGI artifacts it's straightforward; the riskiest are custom attention or fused ops.
[07:45] Samir Patel: We'll flag any custom attention op usage. Most of our production models use standard attention but one research model has a fused block.
[07:53] Maya Chen: If you can share the artifact we can give a go/no-go within 3 business days for small models. For large models it can take longer.
[08:00] Samir Patel: Sounds fair.
[08:03] Priya Nair: Another operational note: do you support canary rollbacks automatically or is it manual?
[08:09] Jorge Alvarez: We have an automated canary system with health checks and auto-rollback/tripwire thresholds. You can configure metrics for rollback like latency, error rate, or quality delta from eval prompts.
[08:21] Rafiq Khan: On the dedicated sizing — our peak concurrency is about 120 rps with average token lengths around 80 tokens. Any rough suggestion for GPU count?
[08:30] Jorge Alvarez: Rough rule of thumb — depends on model size. For 70–80 token average and medium-size models (7–13B), you might start with a 4–8 GPU pool and tune batching. We'll size a recommended config after profiling your traffic and model.
[08:46] Samir Patel: Ok. For the eval parity, can Redwood match the sampling seed environment? We saw sampling differences even with same temperature.
[08:55] Jorge Alvarez: We provide deterministic sampling flags when using autoregressive models and can instrument the same RNG seeds. For sampling-heavy models you might still see variance but it's reduced.
[09:06] Maya Chen: Quick check — any regulatory constraints beyond EU residency? Data residency for APAC?
[09:11] Samir Patel: Not yet, just EU for now but APAC might be next year.
[09:16] Maya Chen: Cool. We'll note that.
[09:19] Samir Patel: One more question — for embeddings parity, we use OpenAI embeddings v2 and have a ton of vector indexes. Moving embeddings breaks search ranking sometimes. How do you handle drift?
[09:31] Jorge Alvarez: We run embedding alignment steps and offer fallback to previous vector index during seeding window. Also techniques like cross-encoder reranking and hybrid search help. For parity we run nearest neighbor recall tests on your index subset.
[09:45] Samir Patel: We'll include a representative index slice.
[09:48] Priya Nair: Sounds good. Any legal / procurement blockers?
[09:51] Rafiq Khan: We'll need standard terms, plus a data processing addendum and evidence for SOC2 and potentially ISO later.
[09:59] Maya Chen: We can provide our DPA and SOC2 + ISO roadmap.
[10:05] Samir Patel: Okay let's talk timeline. We want a pilot in July if possible.
[10:09] Maya Chen: We can start Hosted pilot asap. Jorge, how fast can you run a compatibility probe once they send artifacts?
[10:15] Jorge Alvarez: For small artifacts we can do within 3 business days. For large ones maybe 7–10 days.
[10:21] Samir Patel: We'll prioritize a small model for the probe.
[10:24] Maya Chen: Perfect. Quick wrap — next steps recap.
[10:27] Maya Chen: I'll send pricing and Dedicated SKUs, security packet, and a short onboarding checklist. Jorge will run compatibility probe once you share artifacts. Hedgerow to share 500 prompt subset and a model checkpoint. Schedule technical deep-dive next week.
[10:41] Samir Patel: That works.
[10:43] Rafiq Khan: Thanks all.
[10:44] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
[10:48] [meeting end]

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels and partial words; placeholder timestamps every few minutes. Some domain terms may be slightly off (e.g., 'KV cache' transcribed as 'K V cache' in places).
